title: persona enumerate reports zero sources while the daemon reports one
description:
Empirical confirmation of persona-5s4b.102, observed on macOS 26.6.2 with a real daemon running.

  daemon log:          identity sources active count=1
  persona enumerate:   no identity sources active

Both statements were true at the same moment, about the same machine. They disagree because the CLI probes its own process environment rather than asking the daemon over the socket it just connected to, which is what .102 describes.

This is the shape of bug .102 predicts and the reason it matters: the primary diagnostic contradicts the thing it is supposed to diagnose. An operator debugging 'why do I get no claims' is told there are no sources, while the daemon believes it has one. Neither number leads to the real answer, which is that the one registered source found no tokens.

Filed separately from .102 so the measurement is not lost if .102 is fixed only for the code path and not the disagreement.
close_reason: Fixed in c78a05e. Two defects: (1) 'no identity sources active' counted candidates, not sources, and registry.rs pushes UnixAttestor unconditionally so it was false every time it printed -- that is the .115 contradiction. Counts are now separate. (2) The CLI stops claiming to speak for the daemon. NO RPC was added: the settled constraint is that personad invents no protocol and workload.proto declares one service with no diagnostic method, so the bead's 'add an RPC' fix direction was deliberately not followed. The note also asserts no specific env difference, because a user unit shares HOME and therefore the gpg keyring.
